outcomeNote: single interpretive dictum on the mishna

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, הָכִי קָאָמַר: נָשְׂאוּ גְּדוֹלִים לְאַחַר מִיתַת אֲבִיהֶן – יִשְּׂאוּ קְטַנִּים לְאַחַר מִיתַת אֲבִיהֶן. אֲבָל נָשְׂאוּ גְּדוֹלִים בְּחַיֵּי אֲבִיהֶן, וְאָמְרוּ קְטַנִּים לְאַחַר מִיתַת אֲבִיהֶן: ״הֲרֵי אָנוּ נוֹשְׂאִין כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנְּשָׂאתֶם אַתֶּם״ – אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לָהֶן, אֶלָּא מָה שֶׁנָּתַן לָהֶן אֲבִיהֶן – נָתַן.
segments.en: «Rav Yehuda says» that «this» is what «it is saying:» If «the adults married after their father’s death» and used the common inheritance to pay for their weddings, «the minors» that «marry after their father’s death» may also pay for their weddings from the common inheritance. «But» if «the adults married during their father’s lifetime, and the minors said after their father’s death: We will marry in the same manner that you married,» the court «does not listen to them. Rather, whatever» sum «their father gave» the adults to pay for their weddings in his lifetime «he gave» them, and the minors do not have the right to demand that same sum from the inheritance.

moves.summary: Rav Yehuda reads the mishna as restricted to weddings after the father's death
moves.about: the mishna's rule that minors marry as adults did applies only when the adults married after the father's death

positions.claim: minors may take wedding expenses from the estate only if the adults' weddings were also paid from the estate after the father's death; what the father gave in his lifetime he gave
